title: Cs402 gdb solution
text:
Cs402 gdb solution 

*Answer:* The most favorable machine for recognizing these commands is the **Finite Automaton (FA)**.

The fixed set of voice commands forms a finite language, which is a subset of regular languages. An FA is the simplest and most memory-efficient automaton capable of recognizing regular languages. It inherently reads one letter at a time, making exactly one deterministic move for each letter, perfectly aligning with the device's limited memory, battery, and the requirement for immediate, single-move processing. NFA and TG, while also capable, introduce unnecessary complexity (nondeterminism or string transitions) that would be less efficient for this specific, constrained scenario.

=== Question Title ===

Designing a Smart Voice Assistant: Choosing the Right Automaton

=== Question Description ===

Scenario:

Suppose you are a member of an IoT research team at Virtual University. Your team has been assigned to design a smart home voice assistant named “Nova”. The assistant listens for a fixed set of voice commands:


	“Hello Nova, lights ON”
	“Hello Nova, lights OFF”
	“Hello Nova, fan ON”
	“Hello Nova, fan OFF”


The assistant runs on a small IoT device with very limited memory and battery power. The set of commands is fixed and finite. The recognizer must read the command one letter at a time, make exactly one move for each letter, and decide immediately whether the command is valid (accept) or invalid (reject). A separate module of the device switches the lights and fan on or off. Your task is to propose the most suitable machine for recognizing these commands.

Keeping the above scenario in mind, which of the following machines will be the most favorable?


	Finite Automaton (FA)
	Transition Graph (TG)
	Nondeterministic Finite Automaton (NFA)


Justify your answer with valid reasons.





Read the following instructions carefully before sending your comments:


	Your discussion must be based on logical facts, and in-depth knowledge of the topic is a must.
	Your comments should be relevant to the topic, i.e. clear and concise (maximum 4–5 lines).
	Identify the type of language formed by the set of commands.
	Consider how each machine reads the input (one letter or a string per transition).
	Consider whether each machine is deterministic (one possible path) or nondeterministic (several possible paths).
	Keep in mind the memory and battery limits of the device and the requirement of one move per letter.
	Choose the simplest machine that is sufficient, not just one that works.
	Do not copy your answer from the internet or from other students. Copied or identical answers will get zero marks.
	Post your comment in the discussion board only. Answers sent by email will not be accepted.

text:
